questions.question: Which animal says "moo"?
questions.explanation: A cow says "moo". Sapi berbunyi "moo".

questions.question: Which animal says "quack"?
questions.explanation: A duck says "quack". Bebek berbunyi "quack".

questions.question: The animal that gives us wool is the ___.
questions.explanation: Sheep give us wool. Domba memberi kita wol.

questions.question: Which animal gives us milk on the farm?
questions.explanation: Cows give us milk. (Goats also do, but cows are the most common answer.)

questions.question: A baby chicken is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A baby chicken is called a chick.

questions.question: Andi: "I like horses." Budi: "___" (Budi also likes horses)
questions.explanation: "So do I" is used to agree positively. Budi setuju, jadi pakai "So do I".

questions.question: Sinta: "I like ducks." Rina: "___" (Rina does NOT like ducks)
questions.explanation: "I don't" is the short way to disagree with "I like ...".

questions.question: Tina: "I like rabbits." Lina: "So do I." What does Lina mean?
questions.explanation: "So do I" means "I do too" — Lina also likes rabbits.

questions.question: Read: "Dina goes to the farm. She sees three cows and two ducks. She likes the ducks." — How many ducks does Dina see?
questions.explanation: The text says "two ducks".

questions.question: Read: "Tomi feeds the goats. The goats are white and brown." — What is the colour of the goats?
questions.explanation: The text says the goats are white and brown.

questions.question: Read: "On the farm there are five chickens, two horses and one pig." — How many animals are there in total?
questions.explanation: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8 animals.

questions.question: Rio: "I don't like pigs." Sari: "___" (Sari agrees — she also does not like pigs)
questions.explanation: To agree with a negative ("I don't ..."), use "Neither do I".

questions.question: We borrow and read books at the ___.
questions.explanation: We borrow books at the library.

questions.question: Doctors and nurses work at the ___.
questions.explanation: Doctors and nurses work at the hospital.

questions.question: We can buy vegetables and fish at the ___.
questions.explanation: We buy vegetables and fish at the market.

questions.question: Muslims pray at the ___.
questions.explanation: Muslims pray at the mosque.

questions.question: We send letters at the ___.
questions.explanation: We send letters at the post office.

questions.question: The ball is ___ the two chairs.
questions.explanation: "Between" is used for something in the middle of two things.

questions.question: The cat is hiding ___ the box. We cannot see it.
questions.explanation: "Behind" means on the other side, hidden from view.

questions.question: The school is ___ the mosque and the park. (the school is in the middle)
questions.explanation: "Between" — the school is in the middle of the two places.

questions.question: Read: "Pak Budi goes to the bank to save his money. Then he goes to the market." — Where does Pak Budi go first?
questions.explanation: The text says he goes to the bank first.

questions.question: We can see the teacher's face. The board is ___ the teacher.
questions.explanation: If we see the teacher's face, the board must be behind her (we look past her at the board).

questions.question: Read: "Our school is in front of the post office. The library is between the school and the bank." — Which place is next to the library?
questions.explanation: "Between the school and the bank" means the bank is on one side of the library.

questions.question: A car is parked ___ the gate, so we cannot drive in.
questions.explanation: If it blocks the entry, the car must be in front of the gate.

questions.question: We wear ___ on our feet.
questions.explanation: Shoes are worn on the feet.

questions.question: We wear a ___ on our head.
questions.explanation: A hat is worn on the head.

questions.question: When it is cold, we put on a ___.
questions.explanation: A jacket keeps us warm when it is cold.

questions.question: British English word for "pants" is ___.
questions.explanation: In British English, long pants are called "trousers".

questions.question: What do girls usually wear that boys do not? (Choose one item.)
questions.explanation: A dress is usually worn by girls.

questions.question: Look! She ___ a beautiful dress now.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous: "is wearing" (action happening now). The word "now" is the clue.

questions.question: Tom ___ playing football at the moment.
questions.explanation: Singular subject "Tom" uses "is" with -ing verb.

questions.question: I ___ washed my socks today.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect with "I" uses "have".

questions.question: Look at the boys! They ___ wearing the same shirt.
questions.explanation: Plural subject "they" uses "are".

questions.question: Mother ___ ironed my school shirt.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect: "Mother" (third person singular) uses "has".

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: She have wear a new hat.
options.B: She has worn a new hat.
options.C: She has wears a new hat.
options.D: She have worn a new hat.

questions.explanation: Present Perfect = has/have + past participle (worn). "She" needs "has".

questions.question: My little brother ___ his new shoes right now.
questions.explanation: "Right now" signals Present Continuous: "is wearing".

questions.question: Reading books is my favourite ___.
questions.explanation: Reading is a hobby.

questions.question: I ___ swimming. It makes me happy.
questions.explanation: With "I", we say "I like".

questions.question: Which one is a sport hobby?
questions.explanation: Playing football is a sport.

questions.question: If you ___ rice, you make food.
questions.explanation: We cook food.

questions.question: I love to ___. My pictures are colourful.
questions.explanation: Drawing makes pictures.

questions.question: ___ you like drawing?
questions.explanation: With "you" we use "Do".

questions.question: ___ she play the piano?
questions.explanation: With third-person singular "she" we use "Does".

questions.question: My sister ___ like fishing. She thinks it is boring.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular negative uses "does not".

questions.question: Choose the polite way to say you don't enjoy cooking:
questions.explanation: "I don't really like ..." is the polite way to express dislike.

questions.question: Read: "Riko loves singing and dancing. He sings every day." — What are Riko's hobbies?
questions.explanation: The text mentions singing and dancing.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.explanation: With plural "they", use "Do" + base verb "like".

questions.question: Rina ___ singing, but she ___ drawing.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular: "likes" / "doesn't like" (base verb after doesn't).

questions.question: We can swim in the sea at the ___.
questions.explanation: The sea is at the beach.

questions.question: ___ do you go on holiday?
questions.explanation: "Where" is used to ask about a place.

questions.question: We can see lions and elephants at the ___.
questions.explanation: The zoo has wild animals like lions and elephants.

questions.question: We can see old things from history at the ___.
questions.explanation: Museums display historical objects.

questions.question: The high place with cold air and trees is the ___.
questions.explanation: Mountains are high with cool air.

questions.question: I ___ to go to the zoo this holiday.
questions.explanation: With "I" we use "want". And it is about a future plan, not past.

questions.question: Choose the correct question:

options.B: Where do you go on holiday?

questions.explanation: Question form: WH + auxiliary (do) + subject + verb.

questions.question: We can play, run, and have a picnic at the ___.
questions.explanation: A park is a place for playing and picnics.

questions.question: Read: "Lina wants to go to the beach. She likes swimming in the sea." — Where does Lina want to go?
questions.explanation: The text says "Lina wants to go to the beach".

questions.question: My sister ___ to eat ice cream at the beach.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular "my sister" uses "wants".

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: They wants to go to the mountain.
options.B: They want to go to the mountain.
options.C: They wanting to go to the mountain.
options.D: They want goes to the mountain.

questions.explanation: Plural "they" uses "want" + to + base verb "go".

questions.question: Read: "Andi and his family go to the village. They visit Grandma. Andi rides a bicycle in the rice field." — Where does Andi ride a bicycle?
questions.explanation: The text says "in the rice field".
